title: Introduce buddy-cache allocator with eviction-probing and spillback attenuation
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: reduce long-tail memory fragmentation and noisy-evictions in the KV cache under mixed-size keys/values workloads while avoiding large synchronous spill events. This PR implements a compact buddy-style slab allocator tuned for KV cache objects, an eviction-probing layer that prioritizes low-cost candidate eviction candidates by occupancy and live-score, and a spillback attenuation controller to soften tenant-induced burst spillovers. Key goals: reduce fragmentation, lower p99 eviction latency, and reduce peak disk spill events during traffic spikes. What changed: 1) allocator: introduce src/kv/buddy_allocator.rs implementing a lock-sharded buddy allocator over existing slab segments with coalescing and split hints driven by live occupancy histograms; 2) fragile-score: add a per-page fragmentation scoring heuristic and per-tenant decay window to bias reclaim toward high-frag pages; 3) eviction-probe: new evictor stage that probes short-lived candidate objects using a lightweight LRU-probe path before taking heavy-weight writeback/spill actions; 4) spillback-attenuator: rate-limiter that applies adaptive backpressure to tenants that trigger repeated spill rounds within a short window; 5) observability: new metrics (kv.buddy.alloc_latency_ms, kv.frag_score, kv.evict_probe_hit_ratio, kv.spillback_rate_limiter_actions) and dashboard updates; 6) tests and benchmarks: unit tests for allocator invariants, integration test for spillback attenuation under synthetic churn, and a microbench harness that reproduces production-like size distributions. Performance summary: in CI microbench and internal canary runs we see median allocation latency stable (~20us), 99th allocation latency reduced by ~2.1x vs previous slab strategy for mixed-size workloads, p99 eviction latency improved by ~1.8x, and peak disk spill events dropped by ~35% on a tenant-heavy replay. Risk and rollout: new components are guarded by runtime feature flags (BUDDY_ALLOCATOR, EVICT_PROBE, SPILLBACK_ATTEN). Default remains legacy allocator for safety. Rollout plan: enable for 10% traffic in canary ring, collect frag_score and probe metrics for two weeks, increase to 50% and 100% if no regressions. Backwards compatibility: no wire/API changes. Feature flags can be toggled per-tenant. Related: follows up on ENG-1209 and complements the async spillover controller work. Checklists: - [x] allocator implementation and unit tests - [x] eviction-probe implementation and integration test - [x] spillback attenuation controller and integration test - [x] metrics and dashboards - [x] benchmark harness - [x] doc: design writeup and rollout notes Links: design doc: docs/design/buddy_allocator_design.md. Review conversation: - Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Can you explain how we avoid increased lock contention under high concurrency? The sharded buckets help but I'm worried about corner cases with split/coalesce under contention." - Maya (author): "We use 64 lock shards by default and try-lock in the fast path; split/coalesce use an epoch-based defer queue to avoid holding global locks. I added a microbench that simulates 10k concurrent alloc/free and the allocation latency remained bounded. See bench/microbench/alloc_bench.rs results attached in the PR CI artifacts." - Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Please add a stress test that injects pathological sequences to ensure we don't regress memory accounting for tenants." - Maya (author): "Added tests/kv/allocator_unit_tests.rs with randomized sequence harness and accounting assertions; also added extra asserts behind a nightly-only cfg to avoid perf impact in release runs." - Sofia Alvarez (approver): "Verified canary telemetry for frag_score and evict_probe_hit_ratio in staging; approves for gradual rollout. Left a minor nit on log wording." CI summary and iteration: - Initial CI run: failed unit test due to race in freelist reclaim; author pushed fix in commit maya/buddy/fix-reclaim - Second CI run: all checks passed (unit tests, integration tests, lint, cargo fmt, bench smoke) - Canary run: enabled BUDDY_ALLOCATOR for 10% of traffic in canary cluster; telemetry collected for two weeks with expected improvements; one tenant hit repeated spillback events, attenuator reduced spill rate successfully and an ops runbook was added. Merge: squash-and-merge.
